newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Albright sees new moves to help North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Albright sees new moves to help North Korea.

text.p: With crucial North Korea peace talks due to begin within days, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said Tuesday she expected Japan to provide new food aid to Pyongyang and Asian countries to help fund a landmark nuclear deal.

Foreign ministers at a regional meeting in Kuala Lumpur earlier this week gave no specific committment to her appeal for millions of dollars in funds to help underwrite the 1994 nuclear deal with North Korea, U.S. officials said.

But Albright said she believed "there will be more support for KEDO (Korean Energy Development Organisation) financially than previously ... I thought there was quite a lot of receptivity but we'll see if the check's in the mail."

Asked whether Japanese officials are now more open to extending food aid to meet North Korea's famine, Albright replied: "Yes." She attributed this to Pyongyang's recent announcement that Japanese women who moved to North Korea in 1959-60 and have not been heard from since may return home.
After more than a year of manoeuvring, the two Koreas, the United States and China are to open talks in New York on August 5 aimed at bringing a permanent peace to the Korean peninsuala.
